item.content:encoded:
MLB has witnessed an impressive run from New York Yankees left-hander Carlos Rodon, who is putting together one of the most consistent stretches in franchise history.
The 33-year-old Rodon has not allowed more than three runs in 25 consecutive starts, establishing the longest such streak in Yankees franchise history. His run is also tied for the sixth-longest streak in MLB history, putting his recent performances among the most remarkable stretches by a pitcher.
A historic run on the mound
Oct 1, 2025; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees starting pitcher Carlos Rodon (55) looks on after leaving the game during the seventh inning against the Boston Red Sox during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2025 MLB playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Rodon's latest outing continued that consistency. He allowed two earned runs on four hits while striking out five over six innings against the Minnesota Twins. Despite another solid performance from their starter, the Yankees ultimately fell 5-4 to Minnesota in a marathon 13-inning game.
Rodon's streak dates back to Aug. 1, 2025, when he surrendered four runs over 4.2 innings against the Miami Marlins. Since then, he has managed to keep opposing offenses from scoring more than three runs in every regular-season start.
Strong season for the Yankees lefty
Rodon has also delivered strong numbers throughout the 2026 campaign. He is 6-3 with a 2.95 ERA through 15 starts, giving him his lowest ERA since the 2022 season. That year, while pitching for the San Francisco Giants, Rodon recorded a 2.88 ERA.
His consistency has been particularly valuable as the Yankees navigate the final stretch of the regular season. New York currently holds an 11-game lead at the top of the American League Wild Card standings with fewer than two weeks remaining in the MLB regular season.
The Yankees are still chasing the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East, sitting 4.5 games behind the division leaders. Their next challenge comes Friday, when they begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks.
With the postseason approaching, Rodon's historic streak gives the Yankees another dependable arm as they look to finish the regular season strong.

item.content:encoded:
There is a point where a nice stretch stops being a nice stretch. Carlos Rodón has crossed that line for the Yankees.
Rodón gave them six innings, two earned runs and five strikeouts on Wednesday in Minnesota. The 5-4 loss took some shine off the afternoon, but his start extended a run that is getting hard to brush aside: 25 straight outings with no more than three runs allowed and no more than one homer surrendered.
He does not have to start Game 1. Max Fried and Cam Schlittler have been excellent, and October is not a participation trophy for everybody who had a good September. The rotation conversation cannot be handled with old assumptions anymore.
The Yankees have a real surplus of starters who can make a case. It is a good issue to have, but the first series is short and the opponent decides who gets the ball after the opener.
The Yankees have to count the whole body of work
Rodón’s recent run is not built on smoke. He has kept the ball in the yard, limited crooked innings, and worked deep enough into games to spare the bullpen. Wednesday was not perfect, with three walks and 102 pitches, yet he gave New York a clean six-inning start while the game was still there for the taking.
October asks for exactly that kind of start. Nobody needs a masterpiece every time; they need someone who can keep a game in the middle innings without handing the other dugout a free runway.
I would not overreact to one loss in Minneapolis. I would react to the 25-start sample, because it now carries real weight in the Yankees’ season.
Carlos Rodón has earned a real say in October
The reasonable answer may be matchups. A left-handed lineup could push Rodón up the board, while a series schedule might make a different order cleaner. Fine. The Yankees should use every edge they can find.
What they should not do is treat Rodón like the interchangeable third or fourth starter just because that was easier to say months ago. His work has made the pecking order less tidy. Good pitchers tend to do that.
The rotation debate is not settled, and it should not be. Rodón has made sure it will be an actual decision instead of a formality.

item.content:encoded:
MINNEAPOLIS — Carlos Rodón lanzó seis entradas para los Yankees el miércoles y evitó que se les escapara una tarde complicada, pero las estadísticas finales no lo dicen todo. El zurdo cedió dos carreras y cuatro hits, concedió tres bases por bolas y ponchó a cinco en 102 lanzamientos , en la derrota por 5-4 de Nueva York, en la 13.ª entrada, ante los Minnesota Twins en el Target Field.
Rodón se fue del partido con los Yankees perdiendo por 2-0. Anthony Volpe igualó el marcador con un doble de dos carreras en la novena entrada, y Nueva York se puso por delante tanto en la décima como en la undécima. Minnesota respondió en cada ocasión hasta que un sencillo de Víctor Caratini, como bateador suplente, puso fin al partido en la decimotercera entrada. Tommy Nance se llevó la victoria, mientras que John Schreiber se llevó la derrota.
Con esta derrota, los Yankees quedan con un balance de 88-64. Tampa Bay ganó más tarde ese mismo miércoles, lo que deja a Nueva York a 4,5 partidos de los Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana, a falta de 10 partidos por disputar. Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero las decisiones que tengan que tomar ahora sobre la rotación de lanzadores tendrán repercusiones en la clasificación de la división y en el orden de salida en octubre.
Los resultados de Rodón siguen siendo sólidos. El miércoles sumó su 25.ª salida consecutiva en la que ha cedido tres carreras limpias o menos, todo un récord de la franquicia de los Yankees. Además, ha encadenado dos salidas de calidad seguidas y ha logrado su quinta salida de calidad en 15 partidos, después de haber lanzado 6 1/3 entradas contra los Mets en su anterior salida.
Su carga de trabajo también ha ido por buen camino. Rodon lanzó 102 lanzamientos el miércoles, su mejor marca de la temporada, tras haber llegado a los 93 lanzamientos contra los Mets. Desde que volvió de la lista de lesionados a mediados de agosto, tiene una efectividad de 2,40, un WHIP de 0,93 y una relación de 31 ponches por cada 12 bases por bolas en 30 entradas.
Para los Yankees, sin embargo, la pregunta que surge tras la visita a Minnesota no es si Rodon podrá aguantar una salida. Es si podrá recuperar su potencia habitual lo suficientemente rápido, ahora que las alineaciones de octubre dejan menos margen para una puesta en marcha gradual.
El calendario deja a los Yankees poco tiempo para distinguir entre una fluctuación temporal y una tendencia que se repita.
Los primeros 55 lanzamientos cuentan una historia diferente
La preocupación se notó desde el principio en todo el repertorio de lanzamientos de Rodon, no solo en su bola rápida de cuatro costuras. La instantánea del seguimiento de lanzamientos adjunta a la salida mostraba que sus cinco lanzamientos estaban por debajo de su velocidad media de la temporada tras 55 lanzamientos.
Su bola rápida de cuatro costuras alcanzó una media de 92,6 mph, frente a la media de la temporada de 94,4 mph, lo que supone una caída de 1,8 mph. Su slider bajó 1,4 mph, su cambio de velocidad 2,3 mph, su sinker 1,9 mph y su curva 1,1 mph.
Recurrió a la bola rápida de cuatro costuras en el 45 % de esos primeros 55 lanzamientos y al slider en el 29 %. Eso significa que casi tres cuartas partes de su repertorio inicial procedían de dos lanzamientos que estaban 1,8 mph y 1,4 mph por debajo de sus valores habituales de la temporada.
Eso hace que esa caída inicial sea más notable que el dato de una sola bola rápida. El cambio de velocidad fue el que mostró la mayor diferencia, mientras que ambos tipos de bola rápida estaban casi 2 mph por debajo de sus niveles anuales.
Pero Rodon no se quedó ahí. Su bola rápida de cuatro costuras alcanzó una media de 92,3 mph en la primera entrada, 92,8 en la segunda y 92,4 en la tercera. En la cuarta, esa media subió a 94,9 mph, y más tarde lanzó varios lanzamientos por encima de las 95 mph.
Rodon necesitaba tiempo para soltarse un poco
Rodon habló después sobre su mal comienzo. La información disponible tras el partido no especificaba que esa rigidez se debiera a su codo. Describió cómo se sentía al principio, antes de que su velocidad mejorara a medida que avanzaba el partido.
Rodon dijo que empezó el partido un poco «tenso» antes de soltarse.
Esa formulación es importante por su historial médico de 2026. Rodon empezó la temporada en la lista de lesionados tras someterse a una operación durante la pretemporada para extirparle un espolón óseo del codo izquierdo. Más tarde volvió a la lista de lesionados por una inflamación en el codo izquierdo y se reincorporó el 18 de agosto tras un periodo de rehabilitación.
No se determinó que esa molestia fuera un problema en el codo, y no se informó de ninguna nueva lesión de Rodon tras el partido. Aun así, los Yankees tendrán motivos para estar atentos a la rapidez con la que recupere su velocidad en su próxima salida, tras una temporada acortada por las lesiones.
Los buenos resultados están ocultando una carga de trabajo más intensa
La eficacia de Rodón se ha mantenido intacta, aunque la forma de llegar a las seis entradas haya cambiado. Contra los Mets, el 11 de septiembre, necesitó 93 lanzamientos para completar 6 1/3 entradas, concedió una base por bolas y ponchó a ocho. Cinco días después, necesitó 102 lanzamientos para completar seis entradas, con tres bases por bolas y cinco ponches.
De los 102 lanzamientos del miércoles, solo 59 fueron strikes, algo menos del 58 %. Aun así, limitó a Minnesota a cuatro hits y dos carreras, pero el mayor número de corredores en base y los conteos más ajustados hicieron que esta salida le costara más esfuerzo que su anterior salida.
Teniendo en cuenta sus estadísticas de la temporada hasta el miércoles y su actuación final contra Minnesota, Rodon tiene ahora una ERA de aproximadamente 2,95 en 76 1/3 entradas repartidas en 15 salidas como titular. Los Yankees han contado con él para evitar que el rival anote cuando ha estado disponible.
La salida de los Rays sube el listón
Se espera que la próxima salida de Rodón sea durante la serie de cuatro partidos en casa de los Yankeescontra Tampa Bay, que empieza el martes con una doble jornada dividida en el Yankee Stadium. Nueva York lleva un balance de 3-6 contra los Rays esta temporada.
Ese partido podría ser su última salida como titular en la temporada regular. Además, les da a los Yankees la oportunidad de comprobar directamente si la caída en la velocidad de los lanzamientos del miércoles fue algo puntual o algo que le va a acompañar a Rodon en la postemporada.
Los Yankees obtendrán su siguiente dato cuando le toque lanzar a Rodon contra Tampa Bay, con la lucha por el título de división y la rotación de la postemporada aún en juego.

item.content:encoded:
MINNESOTA — Fresh off the injured list in time for a morning report to the visitor’s clubhouse at Target Field, Clarke Schmidt searched for a pick-me-up on Wednesday.
The Yankees’ pitcher, eagerly anticipating his long-awaited return from Tommy John surgery, wanted nothing more than to take the mound later in the day. But first, he craved a cup of coffee. A latte, preferably.
And if he couldn’t find one?
“Day over,” Schmidt joked. “Not activated.”
It turns out that Schmidt didn’t really need the caffeine, as he was plenty amped up by the time he was summed into the Yankees’ 13-inning, 5-4 loss to the Twins. The first man out of the bullpen — the starter is working as a reliever since he didn’t have time to build up — Schmidt took over for Carlos Rodón with the Bombers down 2-0 in the seventh inning.
It was his first appearance since July 3, 2025.
“It’s a lot like your debut,” Schmidt said. “Thankfully, I’m a little bit more comfortable now, but I think it was similar emotions and a surge of adrenaline.”
Schmidt added that entering the game was “emotional,” and that he had to focus on staying present and slowing things down as he exited the bullpen.
“He looked pretty sharp and didn’t look sped up or overwhelmed at all,” Aaron Boone said. “It’s a tight ballgame there, your first game in over a year, and I’m sure there’s some emotions there. I thought he handled all that pretty well. Hopefully, as he goes now, he’ll get a little sharper.”
That’s not to say that Schmidt didn’t flash potential with the Yankees hoping he can factor into their postseason bullpen. He and Boone were happy with the right-hander’s stuff, and the fact that Schmidt got two swinging strikeouts.
His velocity, meanwhile, topped out at 95.8 mph over 24 pitches.
But Schmidt only got two outs and had to be relieved by Brent Headrick, who got out of the inning unscathed, after allowing two singles. Each knock came on weak contact, but Boone also felt Schmidt’s execution on those pitches could have been better.
Schmidt, meanwhile, was frustrated that he got into three three-ball counts over four batters faced.
Still, the 30-year-old was happy to be an active pitcher again, even if that meant prematurely warming up during a rocky first inning for Rodón.
“In traditional bullpen fashion, I got dry humped a little bit in the first,” Schmidt said with a laugh. “I thought Carlos was coming out, and I was excited and the adrenaline was at a high. And then I had to sit back down and settle down for a second.”
Before and after Wednesday’s game, Schmidt took time to reflect on his long road back from his second Tommy John operation, which he called “not an easy journey at all.” The hardest part, he said, was spending so much time away from the game and a lot of “long, monotonous days” of rehab.
“It was almost like a zero dark thirty-type feel. It’s like you rinse, wash, repeat. You’re doing the same thing every single day,” Schmidt said. “It’s trying to get as much sleep as you can, showing up early in the morning and before the team’s there, and putting all the work in and then staying for the game.
“You learn a lot about yourself spiritually and how to continue to just keep going and keep being resilient.”
Schmidt noted that he leaned on his faith and family a lot to get through the grueling rehab process, so he appreciated that his father, Dwight, a pilot for Delta Air Lines, was able to rearrange his work schedule and make it to Minnesota on Wednesday.
“He’s a trooper, man,” Schmidt said. “[My family] always tries to have one family member at my outings. I’ve been so blessed and so lucky to have a family who’s supportive of me and has been with me every step of the way. I know I wouldn’t be where I’m at without them.”

While it has been a fairly decent year for New York Yankees rookie OF Spencer Jones, an uncharacteristic performance in Wednesday's series finale against the Minnesota Twins at Target Field has put the 25-year-old under the scanner, with multiple fans sharing their concerns and criticizing him on social media.
Jones went 0-for-6 in the series finale, striking out five times, and became the first Yankee to post that record since captain Aaron Judge did so during his slump in 2024. Jones struggled at the plate, prompting multiple fan reactions to his performance.
Here are some fan reactions to Jones' five-strikeout night:
"We can't have this October is around the corner," one fan commented.
"Another bust lol," another fan commented.
The Yankees lost 5-4 in extra innings, missing the chance to secure the sweep in Minnesota. The Bombers fell further in the race for the AL East crown and are now 4.5 games behind the divisional leaders, the Tampa Bay Rays.
Spencer Jones Also Had a Couple of Errors During the Twins Series
On Wednesday night, Jones failed to catch a simple fly ball to center field, allowing Kody Clemens to reach second base. Carlos Rodon showed no visible reaction to the play.
Earlier in the series opener on Monday night, Jones committed a defensive error in left-center field when the ball dipped under his glove, allowing the Twins to score two runs at the plate and prompting a frustrated reaction from starting pitcher Will Warren.
While it might have been a topsy-turvy series for the rookie outfielder, he has ensured that he is worthy of being on the active roster as October baseball nears, with 10 games left in the regular season.

item.content:encoded:
MINNEAPOLIS — Anthony Volpe bateó con tanta fuerza que perdió el equilibrio, convencido de que la pelota se había ido fuera. En cambio, rebotó contra el muro alto del centro-derecha, un doble de dos carreras que igualó el marcador para los Yankees con dos outs en la novena entrada. Durante un momento intenso y emocionante el miércoles, Nueva York parecía dispuesta a llevarse la barrida.
Lo que vino después fueron cuatro entradas más en las que el equipo llegaba hasta la puerta y se negaba a cruzarla. Los Yankees se pusieron por delante en la décima. Volvieron a hacerlo en la undécima. Llenaron las bases sin outs en la duodécima. Cada vez acababan con un empate o con una remontada desperdiciada.
Un viaje que debería haber acabado con una barrida acabó poniendo de manifiesto el único punto débil que un aspirante al título no puede permitirse arrastrar hasta octubre. No se trató de un colapso del bullpen ni de un rebote desafortunado. Fue la alineación de los Yankees la que no paraba de preparar la mesa, pero nunca se sentaba a comer.
La culpa final recayó en un novato que no se la merecía él solo.
Los Minnesota Twins vencieron a los Yankees por 5-4 en 13 entradas, poniendo fin a ese partido maratoniano con un sencillo de Victor Caratini en la primera base que rebotó en el montículo y se coló por debajo del guante de George Lombard Jr. en la segunda base. Con esta derrota, Nueva York queda con un balance de 88-64, a cuatro partidos de los Rays de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, a falta de 10 partidos por disputar. Los Yankees ya tienen asegurada su plaza en los playoffs, pero el título de la división y la exención de la primera ronda se les están escapando.
Una remontada que no llevó a ninguna parte
Nueva York había sumado cuatro hits en ocho entradas y perdía por 2-0, mientras que el lanzador diestro de los Twins, Zebby Matthews, había ponchado a ocho. Entonces llegó la novena entrada. Lombard conectó un sencillo, Paul Goldschmidt le siguió y el corredor suplente José Caballero preparó el terreno para Volpe.
Volpe impulsó las dos carreras, lo que le supuso al cerrador de los Twins, Yoendrys Gómez, su primer salvamento fallido del año y obligó a jugar entradas extras.
Ali Sánchez impulsó al corredor automático con un sencillo en la décima entrada, dando a los Yankees su primera ventaja. Luke Keaschall respondió con un sencillo que empató el partido ante David Bednar. Un fly de sacrificio de Caballero puso a Nueva York por delante en la undécima. Royce Lewis igualó el marcador. Dos ventajas, dos respuestas inmediatas.
La entrada que dará que hablar
La 12.ª es la entrada que los aficionados volverán a ver una y otra vez. Los Yankees llenaron las bases sin outs, la situación que debería haber sentenciado el partido. Pero no sacaron nada de ella.
Heliot Ramos, que bateaba en el turno de Aaron Judge, mandó una bola corta hacia el montículo. Travis Adams la convirtió en una doble jugada 1-2-3. Sánchez se fue con un strikeout, dejando a otros dos en base. Los Yankees acabaron con 7 de 30 con corredores en posición de anotar.
El juez se marcha y el ataque se queda con pocos jugadores
Judge se retiró en la sexta entrada por una contractura en la parte inferior de la pierna derecha que empezó a notar en la primera entrada. Falló dos veces y no volvió al campo, solo siete partidos después de una ausencia de 99 días. Por eso Ramos estaba bateando en su lugar.
El entrenador Aaron Boone describió la noche como una oportunidad perdida, no como un partido robado, y sus palabras reflejaban la importancia del momento en el calendario.
«Obviamente, muchas cosas buenas, pero no las suficientes», dijo Boone. «Ha sido un golpe duro, claro, cuando tenías la oportunidad de barrer la serie y justo antes de un día de descanso. Pero tenemos que superarlo y prepararnos para enfrentarnos a un buen equipo de los Diamondbacks».
Al final del partido, Boone no se anduvo con rodeos con Lombard, pero tampoco lo machacó.
Boone reconoció que la bola de Caratini rebotó en el montículo, pero fue una jugada que Lombard «se espera que haga y sabemos que es capaz de hacer».
Rodón lo da todo en octubre, pero no saca nada a cambio
Carlos Rodón le dio a los Yankees el comienzo que necesita una rotación en la postemporada y vio cómo se esfumaba. El zurdo encajó dos carreras en seis entradas, ampliando su récord de la franquicia a 25 salidas consecutivas en las que ha encajado tres carreras o menos. Lanzó 102 lanzamientos, su máximo de la temporada, y bajó su promedio de carreras limpias a 2,95.
«Empecé un poco lento, un poco tenso», dijo Rodon. «Me fui soltando en las siguientes entradas, así que eso estuvo bien».
Clarke Schmidt hizo su tan esperado regreso en la séptima entrada, ponchando a dos antes de que Brent Headrick dejara a dos en base. El bullpen corrió una maratón que la alineación nunca supo recompensar.
Una primicia para el club que no se veía desde 1991
Este es el dato que pocos destacarán. Ha sido la primera derrota de los Yankees tras ir ganando varias veces en entradas extras desde el 5 de mayo de 1991, en Seattle, es decir, en un lapso de más de 34 años. También fue su octava derrota en la última entrada de la temporada, un récord de la franquicia, y ningún equipo de la MLB ha encajado más hits decisivos en la última entrada en 2026, según datos de Baseball Reference. Ningún equipo de los Yankees ha perdido nunca más partidos a domicilio en entradas extras en una sola temporada.
Lo curioso es que los equipos malos no acumulan cifras como estas. Un equipo mediocre pierde en nueve partidos. Solo un buen equipo es capaz de forzar una prórroga fuera de casa una y otra vez, y luego seguir perdiéndola.
Cómo queda la carrera por la División Este de la Liga Americana
Spencer Jones lanzó su propia advertencia, ponchándose cinco veces en una noche en la que se fue de 0 de 6, lo que demostró lo rápido que se castigan los swings fallidos cuando los márgenes se estrechan. En septiembre se lee de otra manera que en julio.
Los Yankees tienen el jueves libre antes de empezar una serie de fin de semana en Arizona, donde Gerrit Cole será el lanzador titular el viernes a las 21:40 h (hora del Este). No se espera que Judge tenga que hacerse más pruebas. Nueva York ha perdido terreno que quizá no recupere y le ha dado un respiro a los Rays.
Los Yankees saben cómo ganar los partidos intermedios. Una noche en la que solo tenían que ganar uno, no pudieron.

The New York Yankees are now in wait-and-see mode.
Aaron Judge left Wednesday’s game early with right leg tightness. There’s no word yet on whether he’ll have to miss time, and we likely won’t have an answer until Friday at the earliest.
Before then, let’s answer some of your Yankees questions in part one of our mailbag. If you want to ask anything else, there’s still time to do so here.
Note: Questions have been edited for clarity and brevity.
Advertisement
Assuming Trent Grisham is healthy, who starts in center field during the playoffs: him or Spencer Jones? — Ed H.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters Wednesday that Grisham is running “up to a decent speed” in his comeback from a right hamstring strain. Considering Grisham at normal speed is slow, it’s anyone’s guess what that actually means.
If Grisham is ready to go, it will be interesting to see what Boone decides. There are numerous examples of the Yankees opting for the veteran over an inexperienced player like Jones when the games matter most.
Both players have their warts. Neither Grisham nor Jones is a good defensive center fielder. Jones looked abysmal in center, letting a ground ball go under his glove, dropping a fly ball that hit his glove and nearly trucking Heliot Ramos in right field. Meanwhile, Grisham has trouble getting to balls over his head and in the gaps because he’s slow-footed. There’s likely a higher floor of success, though, for Grisham. Even on the balls Jones has caught, there have been instances where he doesn’t look comfortable reading the play off the bat.
So the main difference will come down to offense.
Before Grisham injured his hamstring, he was not hitting. Calls for Jones to take over were already happening. To Jones’ credit, he has produced at the plate. Even after a dreadful 0-for-6 performance with five strikeouts on Wednesday, Jones has a 113 wRC+. He is always a threat to pop a home run, and that wins ballgames in October.
Grisham has one of the best eyes on the team, rarely strikes out and works at-bats. That matters when the batters behind him would likely be Ben Rice and Judge (depending on his health).
Not that my opinion holds any weight, but I’d stick with Jones in center field. The Yankees can always use Grisham, who’s one of the most clutch hitters on the team, in big spots off the bench.
Advertisement
What will/should the Yankees playoff rotation and bullpen look like? I hate to say it, but Gerrit Cole and Max Fried are not looking like aces these days. The team is winning Will Warren’s and Carlos Rodón’s starts. How are these facts likely to influence Boone’s postseason rotation decisions? … As soon as I say this, Fried pitches a gem. Jinx. — Aaron D.
The American League East race isn’t over yet, but the likeliest outcome is the Yankees will play in a wild-card series against the Boston Red Sox. That means the Yankees will only need three starting pitchers for the first round.
Cam Schlittler should start Game 1. There’s no argument otherwise. Schlittler is one of the very best starting pitchers in the sport. You want your best pitcher going in Game 1 to give yourself the best possible chance of not facing a must-win Game 2.
From there, it’ll be a toss-up between Fried and Cole. Both pitchers have concerns attached to them.
Fried has battled command issues all season, while Cole has allowed plenty of hard contact while not getting much swing-and-miss. I’d lean toward Fried over Cole.
As for the bullpen, the Yankees could have Rodón in case the club needs length. The others likely to be on the roster are Will Warren, David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, John Schreiber, Clarke Schmidt, Ryan Yarbrough and Ryan Weathers, if he’s healthy. I’d leave off Tim Hill, who has struggled mightily this season, Luis Gil and Michael Fulmer.
What is the realistic outlook for second base next year? Jazz Chisholm Jr. hasn’t played up to his talent, which might make him more enticing by bringing down his cost. The infield is already crowded, though, with Ryan McMahon under contract, George Lombard Jr.’s promotion, José Caballero, two first basemen (three if Paul Goldschmidt is still seen as Giancarlo Stanton insurance), and Anthony Volpe’s re-ascension. — Marco F.
What the Yankees decide to do at second base is one of the most fascinating storylines of the offseason.
Advertisement
I agree with you, Marco, that this season has likely cost Chisholm millions. He is nearing the end of his worst offensive season since 2021. He won’t reach the heights he set for himself entering 2026, but he still could reach a 20-40 season. Few players have the talent to post those numbers. Before this year, Chisholm posted back-to-back 4+ fWAR seasons. It would not be wrong for the Yankees or another team to bet on his upside.
Chisholm still offers tremendous defense at second and excellent baserunning. If his bat gets back to being considerably above average, he profiles as one of the best second basemen in the sport. There are valid concerns about his offense, though. His hit tool is considerably below average, and as he ages and loses athleticism, that could be a major problem that he cannot overcome.
The Yankees should consider giving Chisholm a short-term deal, though. He is a better option than Caballero and Volpe, who are better as role players, and few available players are better than what he can provide.
The Yankees should strongly consider playing Caballero or Volpe, who played a few games in the minors there, at third base. McMahon is one of the worst everyday regulars in the big leagues this season, and there’s a higher likelihood of Caballero or Volpe producing at the plate.
Has the Martian played his last game in a Yankees uniform? — oconnell13
It’s a hard question to answer because you can’t predict injuries. You never know if the Yankees will have to reach into the minor leagues for depth.
But it’s not far-fetched to think Jasson Domínguez will never play in another important game for the Yankees again. He cannot be trusted in the field. Every game matters for the Yankees, and there’s always a queasy feeling when the ball is hit his way.
His bat also hasn’t progressed enough to keep giving him chances to prove himself. Jones has leapfrogged him on the depth chart, and the Yankees now have Heliot Ramos on their roster. There may not be space for Domínguez.
Advertisement
What are the Yankees’ pitching plans for the rest of the regular season? Specifically, who’s lining up for the Rays series and will any of them be limited in terms of pitch count? — Nick B.
As of now, the Yankees are lined up to start their best four starters against the Rays next week. Here’s how it looks:
Tuesday: Fried and Rodón are in line to start the games of the doubleheader.
Wednesday: Cole
Thursday: Schlittler
The Rays are also on track to start their best pitchers for that series. They could start Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen on Tuesday, Freddy Peralta on Wednesday and Ian Seymour on Thursday. Their rotation is dependent on what they decide to do for their weekend series against the Boston Red Sox. But if they wanted, all of these pitchers could factor into their pitching plans next week.
Any chance the Yanks consider Ben Rice as the backup catcher on the postseason roster to free up an extra bench spot for someone more versatile (and better than) Ali Sánchez/J.C. Escarra? — Matthew L.
The odds of this happening are close to zero.
Earlier in the season, Rice kept catching behind the scenes. Before games, he’d catch bullpens and do on-field drills with director of catching Tanner Swanson. Rice hasn’t done any of that in months.
If anything, Rice would only be used in an emergency situation. Believe it or not, the organization believes in Sánchez. That’s why they didn’t promote Mitch Garver. Sánchez is out of minor league options, so they’d have to designate him for assignment and risk him getting claimed off waivers. They value the consistency he provides to their pitchers, and they think he’s a better defender than the metrics show.

New York Yankees rookie Spencer Jones joined an unwanted club Wednesday, striking out five times in a 5-4, 13-inning loss to the Minnesota Twins at Target Field.
Jones went 0-for-6 as New York's starting center fielder, becoming the first Yankees hitter to strike out five times in a game since superstar Aaron Judge did so against the Pittsburgh Pirates on September 28, 2024. The outing marked Judge's third career five-strikeout game, while Jones recorded his first in the majors.
Talkin' Yanks noted the connection on X, formerly Twitter, one day after Jones hit a three-run homer in New York's 8-1 win.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"Spencer Jones becomes the first Yankee to strikeout five times in one game since Aaron Judge in September of 2024"
Jones entered the game batting .259/.331/.452 with 10 home runs. His hitless afternoon dropped that line to .252/.323/.440, while his strikeout rate sits around 35 percent.
Twins starter Zebby Matthews held the Yankees to two hits across six scoreless innings while recording eight strikeouts. Carlos Rodon countered by allowing two runs on four hits across six innings for New York.
The Yankees did not score until Anthony Volpe delivered a two-out, two-run double in the ninth frame. Both teams scored in the 10th and 11th before going scoreless in the 12th. In the 13th, pinch hitter Victor Caratini singled home automatic runner Luke Keaschall to secure the walk-off victory for the Twins.
The Yankees tied a season high with 17 strikeouts and set another by stranding 13 runners. Their afternoon worsened in the sixth inning when Judge exited with lower right leg tightness after striking out in both at-bats. Heliot Ramos replaced him.

The Twins improved to 71-81, avoided a sweep, and finished the six-game season series tied at three wins apiece. item.content:encoded:
With the postseason less than two weeks away, the Yankees are left holding their breath regarding the status of their slugging captain, Aaron Judge, who left Wednesday’s game against the Minnesota Twins early with what the team described as right lower-leg tightness.
Judge, who started the game in right field, was seen wincing during his second and final at-bat of the afternoon in the top of the third inning following a check-swing. He was pinch-hit for by Heliot Ramos in the top of the sixth, sending up immediate red flags for a team fighting to catch the Tampa Bay Rays for the top spot in the American League East.
Manager Aaron Boone said that Juge felt something in the first inning and took him out to make sure he didn’t “push through anything.”
He will undergo treatment, and the team will get a better sense of how severe the issue is on Thursday.
There may be some relief in that it is not his rib or oblique that is bothering him, though such a statement is a bit premature, considering the specifics of this lower-leg issue is unknown. Judge has already missed three months this season due to a rib injury that kept him out from late May to Sept. 7.
Wednesday’s game was just his seventh game back from the injured list, and he has struggled mightily after the long layoff, going 4-for-23 (.173) with one home run, three RBI, and 13 strikeouts.
Boone previously stated that he was going to take things slow with Judge because they forewent a rehab assignment. But he played six straight games before getting Tuesday off — the day after New York clinched its ninth postseason berth in 10 years.
The prospect of being without Judge this postseason should be a daunting one for the Yankees. Their offense struggled mightily without him, scoring 341 runs in the 84 games without him (4.06 runs per game). Only the Cincinnati Reds, Toronto Blue Jays, Cleveland Guardians, Los Angeles Angels, and Seattle Mariners scored fewer runs in all of baseball during that stretch.
Still, the Bronx Bombers should like their chances regardless of the status of their captain. The American League is exceptionally poor this season, with only six teams possessing records over .500. Three of them, including the Yankees, inhabit the AL East.
They also have one of the most imposing pitching staffs in all of baseball, as they are set to trot out AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, and Carlos Rodon in a shortened postseason rotation.

item.content:encoded:
MINNESOTA — Aaron Judge’s health has the Yankees holding their breath once again.
The slugger left Wednesday’s 5-4, 13-inning loss to the Twins prematurely when Heliot Ramos pinch-hit for him with a runner on and one out in the top of the sixth inning. The Yankees were only down two runs at the time, and Judge, initially expected to rest on Wednesday, was fresh off an off day.
A short time later, the Yankees announced that Judge exited the game with tightness in his right lower leg. The news comes with the right fielder just seven games removed from a 99-day absence for a stress fracture in his first right rib.
“Hopefully, it’s something we were able to catch,” Aaron Boone said after the game.
Neither Boone nor Judge specified what part of the body the latter hurt. Judge, always unrevealing when it comes to his injuries, wouldn’t even say it was his leg, stating he simply had a “lower body” issue.
Judge did say that he first felt something while playing the field in the first inning on Wednesday, but he couldn’t pinpoint a particular play. Boone said he no knowledge of an injury prior to Wednesday, and that he wasn’t made aware of the problem until he noticed Judge hobbling in the outfield on a play he wasn’t involved in during the bottom of the fifth inning.
Judge also appeared to grimace when he took a check swing on the first pitch of his third-inning at-bat.
“I tried to kind of play it off and see how long we could go, because these games are important down the stretch,” Judge said. “But in talking it over, I thought it’d be the right move to come out so we don’t cost the team in the field or on the basepaths.
“I didn’t think it was smart to push it too much here.”
There is no update on Aaron Judge as of this moment
🎥: @YESNetwork pic.twitter.com/hifw6hg9W5
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) September 16, 2026
Judge is facing his latest injury scare with just 10 games left in the regular season. The Yankees have the day off on Thursday before beginning a three-game series at Arizona’s Chase Field, a turfed surface that wouldn’t be friendly to a lower body injury. The second-place Yanks, who have already secured a playoff berth, will then host a crucial four-game series against the division-leading Rays from Sept. 22-24.
With the off day on Thursday, the Yankees will see how Judge responds to treatment. He said “I don’t know” and “probably not” when asked if he’ll get testing, though Boone wasn’t sure about that.
“Hopefully it’s just one little thing,” Judge said, “and then we’re back out there soon.”
Judge likened his leg issue to the types of nagging injuries that pop up during spring training and at the start of the season when players are ramping up their bodies. He has been doing just that since returning from his rib injury on Sept. 8.
“We’re still trying to ramp up, so there’s going to be little things like this that come up,” Judge said. “I just thought it’d be best to — instead of pushing through it like I normally do, and it might become a little worse — get somebody who’s ready to go in there and just try and do what’s best for the team.”
It should be noted that Judge’s rib rehab and pre-activation build-up skipped some steps. He got his wish after repeatedly making it clear that he wanted to forego a minor league rehab assignment despite missing over three months. The superstar also only faced living pitching once, and that came against some minor leaguers.
Asked if Wednesday’s injury made him rethink the process, Judge told the Daily News, “People blow out their calves and blow out their quads in rehab assignments, so I don’t think taking a game in Double-A will change any of that.”
He added that he felt his build-up has been gradual, as he had felt asymptomatic for weeks before returning.
“That’s what we kind of did with playing the [seven] innings, playing the eight innings,” Judge said, referring to his planned early exits in his first two games back, the first of which he said he was “not happy” about the night of.
Judge also had off on Sept. 10.
Prior to Wednesday, Boone had said that he’s been “pleased” with the way Judge has been responding physically since returning to game action. Judge, who has said he wants to be playing every day, said much of the same over the weekend.
The captain, who went 0-for-2 with two strikeouts before departing on Wednesday, hasn’t had much success at the plate since coming off the injured list as he searches for his timing. He did crush a three-run homer in Monday’s victory over the Twins, but he entered that game 3-for-17 (.176) with zero extra-base hits in his first five games back.
Still, the Yankees have been thrilled to have Judge back in a lineup that struggled mightily without him. With Judge’s mere presence impacting the way those around him are attacked, the Bombers had one of the worst offenses in baseball while the back-to-back MVP was on the IL, ranking last in K% (26.1%); 29th in wRC+ (90) and average (.227); 28th in wOBA (.299); 27th in OPS (.681); and 24th in runs scored (341) from June 2 through Sept. 7.
“I’m not sure exactly what’s going on, but it’s never good when your best player on your team comes out of the lineup,” Carlos Rodón said after battling some velocity issues and tightness of his own on Wednesday. “So obviously, I’m hoping he’s gonna be okay. I’m not sure exactly what’s happening, but I’m sure he’ll be fine.”
While it’s too soon to know if Judge will miss extended time, the Yankees will have limited options for his roster spot if that’s the case. There’s fellow outfielder Jasson Domínguez, but he cannot be trusted to play defense in the critical games that are coming up.
Utilityman Max Schuemann is another choice at Triple-A who can also play the outfield.
Of course, the Yankees are hoping it doesn’t come to that.
“Obviously, he’s a key figure to what we do,” Boone said. “Hopefully, we get it treated and knock it out and [he can] be a factor at some point.”

It's been a nice start to the week in the Yankees' home-away-from-home. On Monday night, they clinched a postseason berth with a 7-3 win against the Twins. On Tuesday evening, they fielded the proverbial "hangover lineup" of sorts and still cruised to an 8-1 victory behind a strong start from Max Fried and plenty of strong performances at the plate.
On today's getaway day game in Minneapolis, Carlos Rodón leads the Yankees' effort for a sweep. His most recent start against the Mets was perhaps the best of his season, as he held down the crosstown rivals for one run in 6.1 innings—with eight strikeouts to just one walk. For Rodón, who has for various reasons not pitched deep into games as routinely as he did in 2025, a second straight start of six or more innings would be an excellent sign as he prepares for the postseason.
The Twins, now 4-9 in September, will look to young righty Zebby Matthews, who has turned in an uneven campaign on the hill this season. His past three starts have been illustrative of the step-forward-step-back tendency which has tormented many a young hurler. On August 30th, he twirled an absolute gem, pitching into the ninth inning against the rival White Sox with just one run allowed in a win. His next appearance, also against Chicago, was a far more pedestrian five-inning, four-run effort. Then last time out, he failed to escape the third inning in Detroit—walking four batters and surrendering five runs to hit the showers early.
While the Yankees rested a few of their starters for last night's contest, including Aaron Judge, it didn't prevent them from running up the score. Today, Judge returns to the lineup card, hitting third behind DH Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger, who led the way with three hits and a homer last night. Cleanup hitter Luis García Jr., Spencer Jones, and George Lombard Jr. will make up the middle of the order, with Ryan McMahon, Austin Wells, and second baseman Anthony Volpe (it's still weird to say that) pulling up the rear.

The Yankees’ pitching picture continues to regain its health, as Clarke Schmidt was reinstated from the 60-day injured list on Wednesday as he returns from Tommy John surgery.
The 30-year-old right-hander had been out since July 3 of last season when he was diagnosed with a torn UCL that not only required Tommy John surgery, but also an internal brace procedure. He had a 3.32 ERA and a 1.090 WHIP in 14 starts last season before the injury
He should be in play for a full-time spot in the rotation next season. Over 30 starts between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, he sported a 3.07 ERA and a 1.140 WHIP, which would make an already-great starting five that much more elite.
In the immediate future, though, Schmidt will likely spend this upcoming postseason in the bullpen. Shortened rotations would likely see the Yankees roll with four starters, and there is no usurping Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, or Carlos Rodon.
To make room for him on the 40-man roster, the Yankees designated utilityman Oswaldo Cabrera for assignment. He played just three games with the big-league club this season, spending most of his time with Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. The 27-year-old was slashing .288/.345/.444 in 122 games, but owned a .635 career OPS across parts of five seasons with the Yankees.

NUEVA YORK — Durante casi toda la última década, a Gerrit Cole le tocaban automáticamente los partidos más importantes de los Yankees.
Esa seguridad se ha esfumado.
A menos de dos semanas de que termine octubre, el lanzador que marcaba la diferencia en el equipo se ha convertido en su mayor incógnita. La velocidad sigue ahí, pero los resultados se han deteriorado en el peor momento posible. Aaron Boone ha intentado restarle importancia a la preocupación. Pero lo que pasa sigue haciendo que eso sea cada vez más difícil.
Cole, ganador del Premio Cy Young de los Yankees en 2023, ha encajado siete jonrones en sus dos últimas salidas, la cifra más alta en cualquier racha de dos salidas de su carrera, según MLB.com. El que antes era una apuesta segura para el primer partido ha bajado puestos en la jerarquía de octubre y ha generado un auténtico debate sobre si debería ser el lanzador titular en un partido a vida o muerte.
Para un equipo de los Yankees que tiene el mejor promedio de carreras limpias permitidas (ERA) del béisbol, esto es como una grieta en los cimientos. Nueva York se aseguró el lunes su plaza en los playoffs y ahora tiene un balance de 88-63. El pitcheo es la razón por la que el club cree que puede llegar lejos. Se suponía que Cole iba a ser el pilar de esa fortaleza, no que se convirtiera en su mayor incertidumbre.
Un problema mental que aterroriza a los Yankees
El 6 de septiembre, Cole encajó jonrones de los tres primeros bateadores de los Padres a los que se enfrentó. Fernando Tatis Jr., Jake Cronenworth y Manny Machado conectaron tres jonrones seguidos.
Seis días después, los Mets le dieron una paliza al as de los Yankees en una goleada por 12-2. Francisco Lindor conectó un jonrón con el tercer lanzamiento de Cole. Más tarde, el novato Carson Benge también le mandó la pelota fuera del campo con un slider. Cole aguantó 4 1/3 entradas, encajó cinco carreras y tres jonrones, y se llevó abucheos al salir del campo.
Tras el partido, su explicación hizo que la derrota de los Yankees pareciera aún peor.
Cole tiene una efectividad de 6,08 en sus últimas cuatro salidas, con 17 ponches en 22 2/3 entradas, y ha encajado al menos tres carreras limpias en cuatro partidos seguidos.
En lo que va de temporada, tiene un balance de 8-9, con una efectividad de 3,67 y 20 jonrones permitidos en 115 1/3 entradas. Los Yankees solo han promediado 3,67 carreras en sus salidas, lo que ha convertido partidos que antes parecían pan comido en auténticas loterías.
Lo que realmente preocupa a los Yankees
La preocupación no es que Cole haya perdido de repente su nivel de Grandes Ligas. Es por qué los bateadores se ven tan cómodos frente a él.
Los analistas de YES Network, David Cone y Paul O’Neill, plantearon la posibilidad de que Cole esté delatando sus lanzamientos, lo que podría explicar por qué los bateadores han sabido manejar una bola rápida que sigue alcanzando las 98 mph.
El entrenador de lanzadores, Matt Blake, no lo descartó.
«Es posible», dijo Blake, y añadió que «esa es una de las cosas que vamos a analizar».
Blake también señaló un problema más sencillo. Cole está lanzando strikes a un ritmo sin precedentes en su carrera, pero demasiados se quedan en el centro del strike zone.
«Tenemos que sacar la bola de la parte más ancha del plato», dijo Blake. «Además, quizá tengamos que mejorar la ejecución con dos strikes para lanzar a mejores zonas».
Cole ha reconocido el problema sin pretender haberlo resuelto.
«Hay que empezar a hacer ajustes», dijo Cole.
También rechazó la teoría de que delata sus lanzamientos, diciendo que sus lanzamientos deberían seguir dándonos margen incluso si los bateadores los anticipan.
«Aunque sepan (lo que viene), sigue siendo difícil de batear», dijo Cole. «Mis lanzamientos deberían darnos más margen de error».
Cómo está cambiando la rotación
La mala racha de Cole ha trastocado la jerarquía de la rotación.
Cam Schlittler, en una segunda temporada espectacular, se ha revelado como el mejor lanzador del equipo y un probable candidato al premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana. Se perfila como el abridor del primer partido. Max Fried, que vuelve tras una lesión en el codo, y Carlos Rodón tienen ambos un promedio de carreras limpias por debajo de 3,00 y parecen opciones más seguras para los primeros partidos de la serie.
El enfrentamiento complica aún más las cosas. Es probable que los Yankees se enfrenten a Boston en una serie de comodín al mejor de tres. Cole tiene una efectividad de 5,30 en su carrera contra los Red Sox, y solo los Mets le han bateado con más fuerza.
El veterano columnista Joel Sherman resumió la cuestión de octubre en una sola palabra: «correa». Según su hipótesis, Cole empezaría un partido de mitad de temporada con mucho menos margen de error.
«Creo que Schlittler, Fried y Cole van a ser los titulares», dijo Sherman. «La diferencia es que a Cole le van a dar muy, muy poco margen, algo que, por lo general, no habría tenido».
Sherman también vinculó directamente el techo de los Yankees en la postemporada a que Cole y Aaron Judge recuperen su mejor forma.
«Los Yankees podrían quedarse fuera de los playoffs en menos de 48 horas o podrían ganar la Serie Mundial», dijo Sherman. «Ambas opciones están sobre la mesa y las posibilidades de éxito aumentan mucho más si Cole y Judge se ponen las pilas en las próximas dos semanas, porque son Gerrit Cole y Aaron Judge, y son grandes jugadores cuando están en forma».
Los datos sobre los lanzamientos con efecto explican el colapso
Cole ha mantenido a los bateadores zurdos en un OPS de 0,683. El problema son los bateadores diestros, que tienen un slugging de 0,448 contra él, la cifra más alta que han registrado los diestros en cualquier temporada de su carrera.
Las bolas con efecto del as de los Yankees son las que están causando más daño. Los bateadores diestros tienen un promedio de slugging de 0,652 contra su curva, con diferencia la peor cifra de su carrera. Tienen un promedio de slugging de 0,463 contra su slider, también un récord personal y, con holgada diferencia, su peor marca como jugador de los Yankees.
Además, esos lanzamientos están fallando menos. Su curva solo ha generado un 17 % de fallos contra los bateadores diestros, mientras que su slider se sitúa en el 25 %. Además, está lanzando el slider en el centro de la zona contra los bateadores diestros con la mayor frecuencia de su carrera, lo que explica tanto la reducción de los fallos como los contactos más fuertes.
Los modelos de calidad de los lanzamientos muestran el mismo deterioro. El slider de Cole ha bajado de una puntuación de 125 en Stuff+ en 2020 a 106 esta temporada. La curva de la estrella de los Yankees ha bajado de 120 a 104. Ambas siguen estando por encima de la media, pero el margen que antes le hacía imparable se ha reducido.
Cole cumplió 36 años el 8 de septiembre y está en su primera temporada tras recuperarse de una operación de Tommy John, un año que, según la medicina deportiva, suele ser menos brillante que el segundo. Ya sea por un problema mecánico, por delatar sus lanzamientos o por simple cansancio, Nueva York tiene menos de dos semanas para encontrar la respuesta.
Por ahora, el as que en su día se encargaba de las tareas más importantes está haciendo una prueba para un papel en octubre que antes dominaba.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

#PackPro Carlos Rodón Nominated for the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award
9/16/2026 10:43:00 AM | Baseball
New York, New York – For the second consecutive year, former NC State Baseball pitcher and current New York Yankees starter Carlos Rodón has been named the team's nominee for the Roberto Clemente Award.
 
The Roberto Clemente Award is presented annually to the player who best represents the game of baseball through extraordinary character, community involvement, philanthropy, and positive contributions on and off the field.
 
Each MLB Club nominates a player each year for consideration for the Award in tribute to Clemente's achievements and character. This year's nominees include players whose community and philanthropic efforts have focused on important issues such as raising awareness and funds to support people with cancer and other illnesses or special needs, advancing education for young people, providing natural disaster relief, and expanding outreach to underserved children and communities in the United States and abroad.
 
Fans can vote for Rodón HERE
 
The recognition reflects the Carlos Rodón Foundation's growing reach, the fertility and pregnancy-loss charity he runs with his wife, Ashley, a cause built directly on the couple's own fertility journey.
 
Through their nonprofit, the Carlos Rodón Foundation, Carlos and Ashley provide financial assistance and resources to couples facing infertility and pregnancy loss. As of September 2026, the Foundation has awarded $715,000 in grants to 60 families across 17 states, with 34 families currently in treatment, 15 babies on the way, and four Willow Grant babies born. In just three years, the Carlos Rodón Foundation's annual Willow Gala has raised more than $1.8 million.
 
The August 2026 event alone brought in over $1 million. The foundation has also partnered with Alto Pharmacy to reduce fertility-medication costs for grant recipients.
 
Carlos and Ashley founded the foundation in 2024 after enduring two miscarriages while preparing for in vitro fertilization, an experience that directly led to the Willow Grant, named for their daughter Willow, according to the foundation's website. The grant typically provides $10,000 to $20,000 toward treatment costs for couples who have experienced pregnancy loss, according to the Willow Grant's program page.
 
Ashley has led the foundation's clinical partnerships and its annual gala since the couple launched the gala.
 
Greenwich, Connecticut, declared Sept. 8, 2025, "Willow Grant Day" in recognition of the foundation's work, according to an official city proclamation. The Rodóns have also participated in Yankees HOPE Week outreach tied to the cause, including a visit centered on the nonprofit Bottomless Closet, which helps women prepare for job interviews.
 
Throughout his 12-year Major League Baseball career, Carlos Rodón has achieved several notable milestones, including three All-Star selections, an American League pennant, and MLB's 307th no-hitter in 2021. While the southpaw continues to earn accolades on the diamond, his dedication to service has become just as defining as his accomplishments on the field. In recognition of those efforts, Carlos and his wife, Ashley, were named recipients of the 2025 Joan Payson/Shannon Forde Community Service Award, an honor bestowed on members of the baseball community who demonstrate an outstanding commitment to service.
 
Carlos' commitment to service extends to the baseball community that shaped his life. Through the Carlos Rodón Foundation, he supports two travel baseball teams and one travel softball team, helping young athletes access opportunities that might otherwise be out of reach. Carlos and Ashley also donated to NC State to fund the Carlos Rodón Pitching Lab, a state-of-the-art facility that supports the baseball program's future and gives back to the university that played a pivotal role in his development.
 
"As Carlos is honored to be nominated by the New York Yankees for the prestigious Roberto Clemente Award, we wanted to share a piece of his work that means so much to our program," former head coach Elliott Avent said. "Carlos donated to help create a pitching lab for future generations of NC State baseball, giving young athletes access to a space where they can learn, work, and dream a little bigger."
 
"We're incredibly proud of the work he continues to do on and off the field, and grateful that this program and the people who helped shape him will always be part of that story."
 
Carlos also participates annually in the New York Yankees' H.O.P.E. (Helping Others Persevere & Excel) Week initiative, which recognizes individuals, families, and nonprofits for meaningful contributions to their communities.
 
Carlos Rodón is committed to making a difference both on and off the field. The New York Yankees already have a strong pitching staff.
Now, they'll be adding another veteran arm with less than two weeks remaining in the regular season.
On Tuesday, Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News reported that right-hander Clarke Schmidt will return from the 60-day injured list on Wednesday.
Schmidt, 30, underwent Tommy John Surgery last July and recently completed a rehab assignment.
He made five appearances between Double-A and Triple-A, throwing one to two innings at a time. According to Anthony Franco of MLB Trade Rumors, Schmidt averaged 94.1 mph on his fastball.
In all likelihood, Schmidt will be an option out of manager Aaron Boone's bullpen, not in the rotation.
New York's rotation already has a more than solid top five of Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodon, and Will Warren.
Schmidt made 14 starts in 2025 before learning surgery was required. He posted a 3.32 ERA and allowed a career-low 6.4 hits per nine innings.
To open space on the active roster, right-hander Bradley Hanner was optioned to Triple-A by the Yankees.

item.content:encoded:
On paper, the New York Yankees rotation is set. Cam Schlittler earned his role as the Game 1 starter and AL Cy Young frontrunner, and right behind him is Gerrit Cole, the longtime ace with a wealth of postseason experience. Where things get a little tricky is who comes out for that pivotal swing game, which is Game 3: Carlos Rodón or Max Fried.
If the Yankees were in a healthier position, that question would be easy to answer. It's Max Fried. The issue is that both starters seem to be going in different directions.
In eight starts, Fried looks like he could be regressing. In his most recent start, he pitched 3.1 innings, struggling to get through at-bats against a bad Rockies team. It does feel like he should be at his 100-pitch count already, but his laboring and a decrease in velocity in that start were his biggest red flags. He did strike out seven, and allow one earned run, but his stuff just looked off.
Fried saw a drop in velocity across the board on his cutter, sinker, curveball, sweeper, changeup, and fastball. He saw 2 MPH dips on the sweeper and curve, as well as a 1.2 MPH drop on his fastball.
Rodón is trending upward
Rodón, on the other hand, pitched his best game against the Mets on an emotional night in New York. He threw 6.1 innings with one earned run and eight strikeouts against a Mets team that has rebounded after the deadline. Against Juan Soto and a solid youthful core in A.J. Ewing, Carson Benge, and Francisco Alvarez, he struck out eight, walked just one batter, allowed one earned run, and gave up just three hits. The red flag for his start was six hard-hit balls.
Rodón's velocity was stable, too. He saw a small uptick in fastball velocity, up 0.3 MPH.
Basing the entire trajectory of a postseason rotation on two starts against sub-.500 teams isn't something teams should do, but what happened is worth monitoring in the future. That is especially true if Fried's velocity continues to dip, or stays around where it was against Colorado, without increasing over the next few weeks.
At that point, it would be fair to wonder if Fried could be a liability in October, with Rodón being the better option to be that third starter. The Yankees would probably prefer Fried in that role, but at that point, they should also consider playing the hot hand. If Rodón continues to pitch well and Fried struggles, their performances will answer the question of who should be the third starter in October.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees ace Cam Schlittler added to his American League Cy Young case Sunday afternoon at Yankee Stadium, throwing six shutout innings against the crosstown rival Mets (NYY 2, NYM 0). Schlittler struck out eight and allowed one hit. He is tied with Jacob Misiorowski with a 1.95 ERA, lowest among qualified pitchers, and also with 6.0 WAR, best among all pitchers.
"I think valuable is a good word. He might be the MVP, too," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said after Sunday's game (via MLB.com). "He's been awesome. Just an awesome season and hopefully there's a lot left in the tank."
The is between Schlittler and Dylan Cease, with Parker Messick and Drew Rasmussen trying to nudge their way in as the third finalist. The AL MVP race is more wide open. Yordan Alvarez has hit an un-MVP-like .238/.375/.393 over the last calendar month and his Triple Crown chances are fading, opening the door for Schlittler and others.
Here are the AL WAR leaderboards entering play Monday:
| FanGraphs WAR | Baseball Reference WAR |
|---|---|
| 1. Bobby Witt Jr.: 6.4 | 1. Cam Schlittler: 7.1 |
| 2. Cam Schlittler: 6.0 | 2. Bobby Witt Jr.: 6.3 |
| 3. Yordan Alvarez: 5.8 | 3. Kevin McGonigle: 6.3 |
| 4. Dylan Cease: 5.6 | 4. Dylan Cease: 6.0 |
| 5. Kevin McGonigle: 5.0 | 5. Yordan Alvarez: 5.8 |
McGonigle and Witt play for teams that will miss the postseason, something that has historically hurt players in the MVP voting. As good as Cease has been -- he held the Orioles to one run in five innings Sunday -- he's not having a transcendant "pitcher who deserves to win MVP" season. Schlittler may not be either! He's more in that conversation than Cease though.
One player not on either WAR leaderboard who will factor into the AL MVP race: Rays third baseman Junior Caminero. He's just out of frame (sixth in FanGraphs WAR and eighth in Baseball Reference WAR), but he leads the American League with 40 homers, and he is the best player on the league's best team. That always equals MVP support.
Schlittler has a strong statistical MVP case and probably the best case narratively. He has been the rock in New York's rotation while Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, and Carlos Rodón all missed time with the injury. Also, Aaron Judge missed three months with a broken rib, putting even more pressure on Schlittler (and the team's other pitchers), and he delivered every which way.
Judge, a three-time MVP, wasn't as supportive of Schlittler's MVP candidacy as Boone -- "He's definitely pitching like an MVP, but they've got a Cy Young Award for a reason: best pitcher in the game. He's got my vote, definitely, for the Cy Young," Judge said (via MLB.com).
It's not up to Judge -- or Boone, for that matter. It's up to the MVP voters and Schlittler is at least giving them something to think about.
No pitcher has been named MVP since Clayton Kershaw in 2014. Justin Verlander was the AL's last MVP pitcher in 2011. Kershaw and Verlander both doubled up and won MVP and Cy Young in those seasons. No other pitchers have won MVP since 1992.
Sunday's win improved the Yankees to 86-63. They are four games behind the Rays in the AL East and 4 ½ games up on the Red Sox for the top wild-card spot. New York's magic number is one. They'll clinch a postseason berth with their next win or the Blue Jays' next loss.

item.content:encoded:
Cam Schlittler está casi seguro de llevarse algún trofeo este invierno. Con un par de semanas restantes en la temporada regular, el as en su segundo año parece ser el favorito para el Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana.
Pero mientras Schlittler se prepara para su apertura del domingo contra los Mets, ¿por qué no soñar un poco más en grande?
Si hay un lanzador que merece estar en cualquier debate para el Jugador Más Valioso, es otra figura destacada de segundo año: Jacob Misiorowski de los Cerveceros. Y mencionar a Schlittler no significa que sea igualmente merecedor en el lado de la Liga Americana. Pero no se le puede ignorar por completo.
Considera que al llegar al sábado, el diestro de los Yankees era el líder de la Liga Americana en WAR de Baseball-Reference (bWAR), y estaba cerca de la cima en WAR de FanGraphs (fWAR).
Líderes de bWAR en la L.A. (antes del sábado)
1. Cam Schlittler, NYY: 6.6
2. Bobby Witt Jr., KC: 6.3
3. Kevin McGonigle, DET: 6.1
4. Wilyer Abreu, BOS: 5.9
5-E. Yordan Álvarez, HOU: 5.8
5-E. Dylan Cease, TOR: 5.8
Líderes de fWAR en la L.A. (antes del sábado)
1. Bobby Witt Jr., KC: 6.5
2. Yordan Álvarez, HOU: 5.8
3. Cam Schlittler, NYY: 5.6
4. Dylan Cease, TOR: 5.5
5. Junior Caminero, TB: 4.9
Ocho lanzadores de tiempo completo han encabezado el Joven Circuito en bWAR en los últimos 30 años. Cada uno de ellos ganó el Cy Young, pero solo uno fue reconocido con el JMV (Justin Verlander, 2011).
Schlittler tiene bastantes números que respaldan su candidatura al JMV. Es el líder del Joven Circuito en efectividad (2.01) y ocupa el segundo lugar en entradas lanzadas (178.2), porcentaje de ponches menos boletos (25.4%) y FIP (2.61). Pero su valor para los Bombarderos no se puede interpretar perfectamente por medio de las estadísticas.
Los Yankees han tenido que aguantar lesiones en casi todos los integrantes de su rotación abridora y alineación titular. Por supuesto, la fractura de costilla de Aaron Judge tuvo el mayor impacto para el equipo del Bronx, pero el grupo de pitcheo no contó con Gerrit Cole ni con Carlos Rodón hasta mayo, mientras cada uno trabajaba en su regreso tras una cirugía. Rodón se perdió otras seis semanas a mediados de la campaña debido a una inflamación en el codo izquierdo. Max Fried pasó más de dos meses en la lista de lesionados por múltiples contusiones óseas en el codo izquierdo. Ryan Weathers está actualmente en la lista de lesionados con una distensión en el antebrazo izquierdo.
A lo largo de esta temporada, Ben Rice, Will Warren y Schlittler son los únicos tres jugadores de los Yankees que han respondido de manera consistente. Sin embargo, Rice ha caído en un bache desde la pausa por el Juego de Estrellas, y Warren ha estado solo ligeramente por encima del promedio de la liga (104 de ERA+) en sus 142.1 entradas.
Por su parte, Schlittler ha sido la imagen de dominio y consistencia, prácticamente cargando con todo el roster impactado por lesiones de Nueva York hacia el segundo mejor récord de la Americana (85-63 antes de la jornada del sábado). Ha registrado efectividad de 2.33 o mejor en cada mes de esta temporada, excepto con uno. Ha limitado tanto a bateadores diestros como a zurdos a OPS por debajo de .600. ¿Su efectividad de noche? 2.00. ¿Su efectividad durante el día? 2.05.
Tampoco es que los competidores más difíciles de Schlittler por el máximo honor individual de la Liga Americana estén libres de imperfecciones.
-- Álvarez recibió los 34 votos de primer lugar en nuestra encuesta más reciente de JMV de MLB.com, y si logra completar su búsqueda de la Triple Corona, se escapará con el premio. Pero es bateador designado la mayoría de los partidos, y la realidad es que Shohei Ohtani es el único bateador designado en ser elegido JMV. Necesitó lanzar o registrar una temporada inédita de 50 jonrones y 50 estafadas para lograrlo. Además, la actual lesión de tobillo del cubano Álvarez podría limitarlo tanto en su campaña como en su camino hacia el JMV durante la recta final.
-- Si la temporada terminara hoy, el dominicano Caminero sería el único jugador interponiéndose entre Álvarez y la Triple Corona. Lleva 40 bambinazos para el equipo con el mejor récord del Joven Circuito, mientras que Yordan ha pegado 38. Sin embargo, Caminero, por más dinámico que es en la caja de bateo, es un jugador muy por debajo del promedio a la defensa y en las bases.
-- Witt, quien ha terminado dentro de los primeros cinco en la votación al JMV al concluir cada una de las últimas dos temporadas, podría ser el corredor de bases y defensor más valioso de la Americana. Pero su producción ofensiva para los eliminados Reales (OPS+ de 129) está un escalón o dos por debajo de lo que logró en el 2024 y 2025.
Hace 14 meses, Schlittler no estaba en el radar del JMV de nadie. Debutó en MLB el 9 de julio del 2025 como el prospecto Nro. 12 de los Yankees. Tres años antes, Nueva York lo eligió en la séptima ronda del Draft desde la Universidad Northeastern en Boston. La idea de cara al 2026 era que si podía perfeccionar su comando y control, Schlittler podría desarrollarse como un abridor sólido de mitad de rotación.
Nos podemos atrever a decir que ha superado por mucho esa proyección. Schlittler registró efectividad de 2.96 en 14 aperturas la temporada pasada antes de irrumpir como estrella en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas.
Ha sido esa clase de lanzador élite a lo largo del 2026. Puede que no lo convierta en el segundo lanzador de los Yankees en ganar el JMV, junto a Spud Chandler en 1943, pero el ascenso meteórico de Schlittler, pasando de ser un prospecto de una universidad pequeña a un candidato realista al JMV, es una gran historia por sí sola.
